svg.text: PortalX Pre-Launch Security Hardening | March 2026 | 47 Action Items Across 8 Categories
Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for ALL database interactions — never string-concatenate user input into SQL
Sanitize all HTML output with DOMPurify before rendering — never use dangerouslySetInnerHTML with raw user data
Implement server-side input validation on ALL endpoints using validator.js or Joi — client-side checks alone are insufficient
Apply allowlist validation: define and enforce expected data type, format, length, and character set for every input field
Consider migrating to a type-safe ORM (Prisma, TypeORM) which enforces parameterization by design
Replace MD5 with bcrypt (cost factor ≥ 12) or Argon2id for all password hashing — re-hash existing passwords on next login
Move JWT secret to environment variable; use cryptographically random 256-bit key; validate exp claim on every request
Implement account lockout: 5 failed attempts → 15-minute lockout with exponential backoff; alert user by email
Set all session cookies: HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict — prevents JavaScript access and cross-site transmission
Invalidate session tokens server-side on logout and password change; implement refresh token rotation
Offer TOTP-based MFA (Google Authenticator compatible) as a user option; enforce for admin accounts
Add server-side ownership check on EVERY resource endpoint: verify req.user.id matches the requested resource owner
Replace sequential integer IDs with UUIDs for all user-facing resource identifiers to prevent enumeration
Implement RBAC with clearly defined roles (user, admin, moderator); apply deny-by-default on all routes
Log all access control failures with user ID, endpoint, timestamp; alert on anomalous access patterns
Validate MIME type server-side by reading file magic bytes — never trust the Content-Type header or file extension alone
Re-encode all uploads through Sharp (images) — this strips embedded payloads and normalizes the file
Rename uploads to a random UUID; store outside web root or in S3 with no public execute permissions
Enforce file size limits (2MB), allowlisted MIME types (image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp), and max upload frequency
Add Content-Security-Policy header: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-{random}'; object-src 'none'
Add Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload — forces all traffic over HTTPS
Add X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
Remove Server header; disable X-Powered-By; set NODE_ENV=production; disable debug routes and verbose errors
Add CSRF tokens (csurf middleware or Double Submit Cookie) on all state-changing POST/PUT/DELETE forms
Add express-rate-limit to login, register, reset endpoints (max 10/15min)
Use HTTPS-only API endpoints; enforce TLS 1.2 minimum
Return generic error messages — never expose internal errors to clients
Run npm audit --fix; patch axios, lodash, multer CVEs now
Enable Dependabot or Snyk for automated PR alerts on new CVEs
Integrate SAST (Semgrep / ESLint-security) in CI/CD pipeline
Deploy WAF (AWS WAF / Cloudflare) before public launch
Run OWASP ZAP scan on staging before every release
Log auth failures, access violations, anomalous exports
Publish responsible disclosure / bug bounty policy at launch
Mandatory (MAND): 8 items | High (HIGH): 10 items | Recommended (REC): 14 items | Best Practice (BP): 8+ items
All MANDATORY items must be checked ✓ before launch sign-off. MAND + HIGH = minimum viable security baseline.
PortalX Web Application Security Audit · March 2026 · Application Security Division · CONFIDENTIAL
